objective: Prevent the measured punctuation and subword collapse that remains after rejection of the lexical guard while preserving all quality-passing validation outputs and the native CPU advantage.

controlling_evidence.measured_failure: Three byte-target outputs remained above the locked 0.60 byte four-gram repetition ceiling through punctuation or single-character loops despite lexical-loop blocking.
controlling_evidence.quality_safety_margin: Among 1,400 quality-reference outputs, every passing output has byte four-gram repetition at or below 0.5103448275862069. Only two already-failing grammar outputs exceed 0.60.

candidate_lock.selection_rule: After 32 generated bytes, reject a greedy candidate token only if accepting it would cross the locked 0.60 byte four-gram repetition ceiling; select the next highest logit. If an existing prefix is already above the ceiling, accept only a candidate that does not worsen it.

decision_rule: Implement and screen exactly one byte ceiling and one activation length fixed above. Reject rather than sweep either value if the complete validation suite or repeated CPU benchmark fails.
claim_boundary: This is a generic deterministic collapse guard aligned to the locked output-quality metric. It adds no English knowledge and does not prove teacher equivalence.
